## Execution audit

**Provenance.** Let `P` denote `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/`. Expanded files cited below are under `P/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/`; their corresponding archive members are under `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/` with the same suffix. The archives are `P/work/scene_archive/bundles/r2--fixed_h0.tar.gz` for fixed-H0 files and `P/work/scene_archive/bundles/r2--generic_rsi.tar.gz` for generic-RSI files. Citations give source ID, suffix, and original line numbers.

### Dormitory — fixed H0, commons_163096530

Step 1 failed before producing an image: `world.use_nodes` raised an AttributeError because the world was `None` (X0958, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). Step 2 explicitly creates a world if absent. Its generated scene uses individual boards and grain strips, plaster and timbers, three left bunk assemblies with separate posts, rails, mattresses, sheets and ladders, a wardrobe, fireplace, guard and foreground bunk (X0959, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/steps/002/build.py`, lines 16–101, 103–180, 195–224).

The code sets roughness to .79 and attempts noise-driven bump on materials encountered on named surfaces; it tracks processed material names, so assignment depends on encounter order. It specifies a 31.5 lens, two area emitters, ambient world, Cycles and 512×341 PNG, with 48 samples (X0959, lines 226–275). Actual step 2 succeeded and saved PNG and blend files, but the render log reports **16/16 samples**, not the scripted 48 (X0960, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7). The reference metadata is 512×341 (X0963, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/task.json`, lines 2–5); that is not an independently measured output size.

Step 3 changed the floor, bunk positions and foreground crop, added ceiling flakes and color-conditioned metallic or procedural grain/bump materials, and specified lens 39 and 64 samples with denoising (X0961, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/steps/003/build.py`, lines 16–52, 54–98, 173–203, 207–271). It timed out after about 464 seconds with no reported image; its intended changes cannot be treated as a completed render (X0962, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). No selection or acceptance record for this scene was supplied.

### Woodworking room — fixed H0, commons_199974832

The generated design represents shelves of many separate hand planes, chisels and hanging tools, plus a crowded workbench with saws, containers and screw trays. Planes use separate bodies, soles, inclined blades, wedges and swept handles; instances are rotated and translated (X0968, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/steps/002/build.py`, lines 34–120, 129–165, 167–257). Its wood-like colors receive mapped noise, a color ramp and bump; near-neutral dark colors receive metallic shading. The code specifies a 31 mm lens, three area lights, a guarded ambient world, Cycles, 48 samples and 512×384 output (X0968, lines 261–317; reference dimensions: X0970, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/task.json`, lines 2–5).

Step 1 failed on `sc.world.color` because the world was `None` (X0967, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). Step 2 added world creation but timed out after about 425 seconds, without an image (X0969, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/steps/002/result.json`, lines 2–7). The record reports failure, missing blend or PNG, null similarity metrics, false functional checks and no selection; it classifies the failure as budget or scene timeout (X0964, `fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_199974832/record.json`, lines 16–35, 46–54). This is a technical failure, not evidence that a completed reconstruction looked poor.

### Chaise — generic RSI, commons_109923183

The final expanded build describes a separate cushioned seat, resized and rotated padded headboard, swept frame, arms, aprons and legs, pillow, label and cropped cane chair. Its comments claim a prior head was too narrow and high; that is author assessment, not independently verified visual evidence (X0971, `generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/build.py`, lines 5–12, 46–125, 139–155). It uses wave-and-noise upholstery shading and a rotated brick/noise oak material, assigned to meshes whose world bounding-box tops are below .01; this criterion is not a contact or semantic test (X0971, lines 160–233). Camera is `(1.05,-4.25,3.15)`, lens 50, with two area lights and AgX (X0971, lines 10–12, 235–244).

Step 1 demonstrably rendered, logging 418 primitives and 16 samples (X0976, `generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). The separate selection file records step 3, although the record’s `selected` field is null (X0973, `generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/selected.json`, lines 1–3; X0972, `generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/record.json`, lines 53–57). The record reports completion, validity, overall 0.3998 and functional passes; those checks explicitly concern structural/edit operability, while semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null (X0972, lines 16–34). No images were supplied for visual inspection. Coordinates, bounding boxes, successful rendering and numeric scores do not establish part contact or image fidelity; the completed chaise may still be a poor reconstruction.
